summary: A comment is a note for people reading your code. Python skips it when the program runs.
notes: # starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
A string in triple quotes at the top of a file is a docstring. It describes what the file does.
__doc__ holds the file's docstring. Putting # in front of a line of code turns it off without deleting it.
pitfall: Using // for a comment, as in Java, causes SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Python comments use #.
